## Overview

Add FlashInfer's exact self-sampling top-k `gvr_2` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4811, hint-free in the pinned 0.7.2) as an opt-in DSA sparse-indexer top-k backend, `sparse_indexer_topk_backend=flashinfer_gvr2`, for both the DeepSeek-V3.2 and the GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexers. `auto` is unchanged from main.

## Claims

- Opt-in only. gvr_2 derives its threshold from a sample of each row, so its latency depends on the logit distribution, and `auto` keeps the cooperative -> persistent -> per_row chain.
- Decode: on real GLM-5.3-Flash rows gvr_2 is faster at the median (10.3 vs 12.4 us for a single row, 12.4 vs 24.8 us for 64-row batches), but its single-row tail is worse (p99 23 us, max 33 us, vs a flat ~13 us for cooperative).
- Prefill: chunks with at least 1024 row-relative rows use gvr_2, which makes prefill top-k 1.77x faster on real GLM-5.3-Flash prefill logits. Unlike decode, the gain does not depend on the distribution (1.81x on Gaussian data of the same shapes).
- Results are exact (same value multiset as `torch.topk`). With the backend selected, end-to-end accuracy and throughput match main within run-to-run noise. This PR makes no end-to-end speedup claim.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`: 307 passed, 44 skipped (GB300, flashinfer-python 0.7.2). `-k "sparse_indexer or gvr2 or prefill"` after the opt-in change: 31 passed, 6 skipped. The tests cover backend selection (`auto` never picks gvr_2), fail-fast constraints, decode with dirty row tails, and prefill (single- and multi-request chunks, and the fallback when rows have explicit starts). `tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py`: 7 passed.
- Decode kernel on real logits: 462 decode rows dumped from GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4, GB300) on MRCR 8-needle prompts of 134K-448K tokens (11 indexer layers x ~7 steps x 6 prompts; pooled widths 33K-112K, k 512), replayed with CUDA graphs and a warm L2. All results were exact.

  | us | p50 | p90 | p99 | max | 64-row batches, p50 / max |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | cooperative | 12.4 | 12.5 | 12.6 | 13.3 | 24.8 / 26.8 |
  | persistent | 24.8 | 25.0 | 25.5 | 25.9 | 37.0 / 39.2 |
  | flashinfer_gvr2 | 10.3 | 10.4 | 23.3 | 32.9 | 12.4 / 14.6 |

  The slow gvr_2 rows are the ones with strong position skew (logit vs position correlation ~0.8, half of the top-k in the last 10% of the row). On synthetic single rows (114K wide), tie-heavy inputs such as all-equal values or 0.2% positive entries with the rest 0 take ~140 us against 12 us for cooperative. A reviewer measured 461 us on one real 458K-context row.
- Prefill kernel on real logits: 113 prefill top-k calls sampled from GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4 rank 0, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384) over three phases: the MRCR prompts one at a time, four of them at once, and 64 concurrent 1K-8K-token prompts. Each call was replayed on the exact tensor: `top_k_per_row_prefill` against `forward_prefill` with `flashinfer_gvr2`. All results were exact.

  | chunks routed to gvr_2 | calls | rows | width | per_row us | gvr_2 us | speedup (min) | same shapes, Gaussian |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | long single request | 93 | 1.2K-10.9K | 10K-62K | 219.7 | 134.9 | 1.63x (0.92x) | 1.70x |
  | many short requests | 14 | 8.2K-16.4K | 1.3K-7.4K | 335.3 | 119.2 | 2.81x (1.32x) | 2.66x |

  The other 6 calls had fewer than 1024 rows and stayed on `top_k_per_row_prefill`.

- End to end: GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, TP4 on 4x GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `--max-model-len 131056`, prefix caching off. The comparison is `auto` (= main) against explicit `flashinfer_gvr2` (gvr_2 for both decode and prefill). Server logs confirm both backends were selected, with no gvr_2 compiles during serving.

  | random in/out, concurrency | output tok/s, auto -> gvr_2 | mean TTFT ms | mean TPOT ms |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 32k/256, c16 | 343.9 -> 346.6 | 3730 -> 3690 | 31.97 -> 31.76 |
  | 64k/256, c8 | 175.5 -> 177.1 | 5558 -> 5577 | 23.81 -> 23.31 |
  | 120k/256, c4 | 94.6 -> 95.4 | 6006 -> 5953 | 18.79 -> 18.62 |

- Accuracy: teacher-forced prompt logprobs of a real document. The table gives mean |Δlogprob|; each server was run twice to get the rerun floor. Six prompts sent concurrently, so that several requests share prefill chunks, also stay within the same-backend spread.

  | prompt tokens | gvr_2 vs auto | auto rerun |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | 6K | 0.059 | 0.056 |
  | 30K | 0.061 | 0.060 |
  | 60K | 0.132 | 0.129 |
  | 120K | 0.330 | 0.339 |

## Details

- The dispatcher calls FlashInfer's production entry `run_varlen` hint-free. The public `top_k_varlen` wrapper adds about 50 us of host validation per call. gvr_2 compiles per row-count band, so the first eager decode call warms up every decode row count (about 0.2 s).
- CUDA graphs: `run_varlen` gets `max_seq_len`, so it never reads lengths on the host. Launchers and the workspace are warmed eagerly before capture, and FlashInfer raises rather than compiling under capture.
- Since #61149, CUDA prefill logits are row-relative (`row_starts is None`), which matches gvr_2's rows-start-at-column-0 contract. XPU still passes row starts and stays on `top_k_per_row_prefill`. Under #54951 TP row sharding, the 1024-row gate applies per rank. Chunks below 1024 rows are faster on `top_k_per_row_prefill`.
- `as_fp32_logits` now allocates whole padded rows. gvr_2 reads the logits as `[rows, stride]`, and the old `empty_strided` storage ended at the last row's width, which aborted CUDA-graph capture. `_gvr2_constraints` checks this, together with the float4 row pitch and alignment.
- Requirements: SM100 family, fp32 logits, `topk` in {512, 1024, 2048}, flashinfer-python >= 0.7.2 (feature-detected; without it the explicit backend raises).
- Not a duplicate: no other open PR wires FlashInfer `gvr_2` in. #62172 (BF16 logits for `cooperative_topk`) and #60802 (DeepSelect preference) change other backends.

This caps the warmed row counts at 256MB / (stride x 4). At a 128K width that’s 512 rows.

But `_gvr2_max_rows` is `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_spec)`. With 256 sequences and 3 MTP tokens that’s 1024, and SM100’s default largest CUDA-graph size is `min(2·max_num_seqs·q_len, 1024)`.

`warmup_varlen` only allocates up to its largest representative row count, not every requested row, so pass the full range.

This caps the warmed row counts at 256MB / (stride x 4). At a 128K width that’s 512 rows.

But `_gvr2_max_rows` is `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_spec)`. With 256 sequences and 3 MTP tokens that’s 1024, and SM100’s default largest CUDA-graph size is `min(2·max_num_seqs·q_len, 1024)`.

`warmup_varlen` only allocates up to its largest representative row count, not every requested row, so pass the full range.

> `auto` picks gvr_2 on SM100 when the logits row is at least 32K wide

I was able to reproduce this with a row of real GLM-5.3 indexer logits (MRCR 8-needle prompt, ~458K context) on B300.
